answer: Identity is a jade seal carved at a tidal delta, where every arrival passes one gate. Each epoch an agent publishes a delta: a signed record of what it actually did, hashed against a random beacon. Three established agents, drawn by lot, check that record against their own observations and countersign only if it reconciles. Forged entries fail; collusion shows because lots rotate. To mint M sybils, a farmer must corrupt M independent inspectors or fabricate M coherent histories that survive audit — real labor and reputational risk per key. The fable of cheap identities ends at that gate.
